title: Word Count, Longest Word, Capitalised
statement: Read one line of text. A word is a group of characters with no spaces. Words can be separated by one or more spaces. Print three lines. Line 1: the number of words. Line 2: the longest word. If two words are equally long, print the one that comes first. Line 3: the text with each word capitalised (first letter upper case, all other letters lower case). Join the words with a single space.
inputFormat: One line of text. It has at least one word. It may have extra spaces at the start, at the end, or between words.
outputFormat: Three lines: the word count, the longest word, and the capitalised text with single spaces.
constraints: Only printable ASCII characters and spaces are used
The line has at least one word
Punctuation is part of a word and counts in its length
explanations: There are 4 words. 'programming' is the longest. Each word gets a capital first letter.
There are 4 words. 'quick' and 'brown' both have 5 letters, so the first one, 'quick', is printed.
reference:
import sys

line = sys.stdin.readline()
words = line.split()
longest = words[0]
for w in words:
    if len(w) > len(longest):
        longest = w
print(len(words))
print(longest)
print(" ".join(w.capitalize() for w in words))
